About this species: Atriplex halimus, commonly known as Mediterranean saltbush, is a perennial salt-tolerant shrub of arid and semi-arid lands. It grows well in saline soils, coastal zones, degraded rangelands, and dry inland habitats. The plant is widely valued as drought- and salt-tolerant fodder, especially in dryland grazing systems. Its greyish leaves and woody branching help it survive harsh conditions and make it useful for soil stabilization, rangeland rehabilitation, and saline-land management.
Geographical distribution: Macaronesia and Mediterranean region to W Iraq, NE Tropical Africa and Arabian Peninsula
